newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA rises after strong half yr result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA rises after strong half yr result.

text.p: The shares of Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) rose strongly from the start of trade on Wednesday after the company reported strong half year earnings and said it expected a slightly better than expected result for the year to June 30, 1997.
At 10.10 a.m (2310 GMT), CBA shares were 29 cents or 2.2 percent firmer at A$13.70 on turnover of 430,240, just nine cents short of its life high of A$13.78, set on Monday.
Earlier, the bank said that its 11 percent rise in net profit to A$602 million for the six months to December 31, 1997 was due to better than expected growth in business volumes.

"It (the result) was better than expected. Top of the (analysts' forecast) range was about A$550 million and at just above A$600 million and an increased dividend means the stock is all the rage this morning," said Jamie Spiteri, a dealer at Shaw Stockbroking.
CBA lifted its interim dividend payment to 45 cents from 38 cents in the previous corresponding period.
